name: paper-grain invisible on near-black fields (additive option / lift dark bumpers)
description: From the text-3d Critic (2026-06-21, non-gating aesthetic-miss). paper-grain is MULTIPLICATIVE (out = rgb*(1±0.06*density)); on a near-black backgroundFill like #040408 (luma ~0.018) the per-frame shimmer is ~0.0002 luma = below visibility. So even after the effect-chain fix (grain now reaches the opaque backgroundFill), the grain reads as nothing on dark bumpers — verified background-only region 0 changed px on text-3d. The dark full-frame bumpers (text-3d, counter, instance-stack, cursor-trail, all on #040408) get NO living grain layer. Options: (a) add an ADDITIVE grain mode/term so grain is visible on near-black, or (b) lift the bumper fields slightly off pure-black (graded backdrop) so multiplicative grain + tone have something to live in. Pairs with the systemic 'flat CSS on black' audit deficit — these 4 bumpers have flat #040408 voids vs the graded backdrops the surfaces got. Low priority; the bumpers are Critic-ACCEPTed (foreground motion carries their holds).
result: Option (a) shipped: paper-grain gains a lift param (zod default 0 → byte-identical for every existing composition; x + 0·grain is bit-exact). lift couples the same two-octave grain field ADDITIVELY, weighted (alpha − luma) — full on opaque near-black, zero on bright content and transparent pixels (premultiplied-correct, E4 holds). Editor slider shipped with it (parity); pack() guards missing lift with ?? 0 for the raw-manifest pack-chrome lane. The three dark bumpers still authoring grain (counter-milestone, cursor-trail-title-sweep, instance-stack-vertical) author lift 0.3; text-3d no longer carries grain post-re-dress. Verified on counter-milestone 4K CDP captures: field liveness went 2% of px (dither-level, the dead field this task described) → 48% at max ±2/255; delta-by-luma monotone 0.37→0.09; amplified crops show organic structure that also masks field banding; frame at 1x still reads flat warm-black (Q12/brand-safe). description: Known limitation shipped with 6ltfmkwx (noted in newspaper CanvasSource + crt manifest): the newspaper's edge is now intrinsically torn, so its CSS depth branch is dead and the pack's newspaper depth claim reaches pixels only through the edge-treatment ShaderPass's synthesized shadow — which handles hardOffset rigs only. crt-terminal's core glow depth therefore does not reach the clipping at all (no bloom rim on newspaper under crt; previously crt claimed edge 'none' and took the CSS glow branch). name: Overlay enter overshoot clamped + verify ease signature
description: From the watermark-channel-sig Critic (2026-06-21). OverlayMount.svelte visibilityStyle clamps overlay enter/exit progress to [0,1] (Math.max(0,Math.min(1,progress))), so any back.out/settled overshoot the engine computes into animState.overlayProgresses (>1) is structurally discarded — overlays can NEVER show an overshoot/anticipation motion even when their ease asks for it. Surfaces have the analogous fade-only enter (paperVisibility opacity ramp). (1) Decide: should overlays support overshoot motion (un-clamp + drive a transform, not just opacity), or is fade-through the intended overlay motion-form? The watermark identity declares fade-through, so for it the fade is correct — but the clamp is global. (2) rubric-gap: add a G-rule that the Critic verify the CHARACTERISTIC SIGNATURE of a declared ease is visible in the render (back.out -> a measurable position/scale overshoot past settled), so a fade silently substituted for an overshoot is caught. Non-gating.
result: Resolved (no engine change — clamp is correct). Investigated the OverlayMount [0,1] enter-progress clamp the watermark Critic flagged. Conclusion: it is INTENTIONAL and correct — every overlay Pipeline declares a fade-through / intrinsic motion-form (watermark explicitly 'fade-through'; counter/instance-stack/cursor-trail/shader-fill/lower-third have intrinsic motion-forms driven by mount enter timing). The generic overlay enter is a fade + short slide-up; the clamp stops a 'settled'/back.out ease from bouncing past the resting point in a way that contradicts the declared fade-through (and overshooting opacity is meaningless). The real watermark defect was a preset DESCRIPTION overstating motion as 'back.out overshoot' — already corrected to render-truth. Added a clarifying comment in OverlayMount.visibilityStyle so it isn't 'fixed' later. Enabling overshoot would be a separate per-overlay motion-form opt-in feature, not needed now. The ease-signature-verification idea is already effectively performed by Critics (the watermark Critic caught exactly this mismatch via render-is-truth).

description:
THE one systemic finding from the hpc3lrk0 pack-matrix sweep (2026-08-04, .tmp-critique/pack-matrix/index.html; 42 deliverables x 4 packs, everything else judged clean or Scott-borderline). One failure class, two shapes:

(a) AUTHORED light ink on a pack-driven field: docu-flowchart (inkColor #f4ecdc), docu-timeline-build, wake-conversation-flow, text-3d-cylinder author light ink for their formerly-authored dark fields; with backgroundFill:'pack' the FIELD follows the pack, so under clean-light (#f6f7f8) the authored light ink is invisible (white-on-white edges/labels/titles).

(b) PER-PIPELINE label/node ink claims calibrated for card-grounds: editorial-mono's diagram/label inks are dark (calibrated against its cream cards), so full-frame diagram pieces on its dark field (#080b10) render near-invisible (dark-on-dark).

Borderline same-class: docu-stat-build under editorial (dim), counter-milestone under clean-light (faint white digits).

Root: field-treatment (ADR-0039 S3) gave the FIELD a pack home but nothing pairs an INK to the field — core ink-treatment is the DOCUMENT ink (dark on light stock), wrong for text sitting directly on a dark field. Design direction to grill: a companion optional core (field-ink-treatment) resolved wherever content sits on the field (diagram labels, full-frame titles, counter digits), + lift the authored light-ink restatements from the affected presets so the pairing drives. Alternative considered: luminance-adaptive ink (contrast-flip against resolved field) — less authorable, breaks render-is-truth explicitness. The quality-arc workstream that owned the diagram-register rebuild (vgi2krdc) completed 2026-08-04; this finding now stands alone as roadmap runway item 3 — same affected pieces, design-first.

Judgment item riding along for Scott: crt-terminal's scanline material rasters quoted paper documents (research papers, news mocks get a faint raster). By design (material treats the merged frame; probe exempts it) but worth a keep/exempt ruling — disablePackMaterial exists as the opt-out lever per surface.
result: Shipped explicit Pack field/ink pairing. Added optional field-ink-treatment resolution for direct-on-field Diagram ink, plain full-frame Surface text, and plate-less full-frame Overlay ink, with authored ink first and ordinary ink fallback; no runtime luminance adaptation. Added calibrated field ink to all four Packs, removed affected authored light-ink restatements, and preserved card/document ink, Pack immunity, node interiors, and transparent-over-footage behavior. Verification: npm run check passed; 78 Vitest files/370 tests passed; focused field-ink tests 26/26; structural and preset corpus gates passed; policy-sweep 5/5; every registered Pipeline passed region-attributed Pack diff across four Packs; 24 native 3840x2160 captures completed with zero browser/WebGPU/network/console errors. name: Emit Factory effectiveness through Sentry Application Metrics
description:
## Goal
Send bounded, deterministic Factory flow measurements to one dedicated Sentry Application Metrics project so effectiveness trends compare repositories and Factory profiles beside their operational telemetry.

## Current capability
The repo uses @sentry/sveltekit 10.67.0; Application Metrics are supported from 10.25.0. The canonical source remains @mgreten/software-factory-flow-metrics output.

## Architecture
No local or registry Swamp Sentry model existed as of 2026-08-05. Do not emit network side effects from a report and do not wrap the Sentry CLI in command/shell. Build a typed emitter model using the Sentry SDK and a vault-backed DSN for a dedicated Factory-observability Sentry project. It accepts only the bounded terminal-run payload, emits metrics, flushes before exit, and records a versioned success/failure result. Sentry is a trend surface, never a Factory gate.

## Comparison dimensions
Every metric carries factory.project (explicit stable project slug, never an absolute path), factory.name (local instance), factory.profile (reusable profile name/version), and factory.definition_version. Never emit work item ids, paths, actors, repo URLs, or other unbounded identifiers.

## Metric contract
- factory.run.completed count with outcome/project/factory/profile/definition/first-pass/visual attributes.
- factory.run.duration and factory.stage.duration distributions in milliseconds.
- factory.run.dispatch_attempts, factory.run.human_decisions, and factory.run.patch_cycles distributions.
- factory.run.cleanup_failure count only for cleanup-required outcomes.
- factory.metric.coverage gauge for bounded unavailable/available facts.

## Done when
The emitter model is schema-validated and fixture-tested, one terminal Factory summary produces queryable Sentry metrics and a versioned Swamp emission result, dashboards can group and compare by project/factory/profile, missing DSN is explicit/non-gating, duplicate emission is idempotent, and docs/project-control-plane.md remains accurate.

name: Canvas-inspired optical and deformation capability arc
description:
## Goal
Build a clean-room Supers-native family of optical, reveal, deformation, and simulation capabilities inspired by observed CanvasUI behaviors, without importing or porting CanvasUI source, shaders, defaults, assets, or components.

## Why
The current magnify Annotation is visually weak, and the current glass vocabulary is limited to fluted architectural glass. Supers should add physically legible lens/frost/refraction treatments plus deterministic particle, peel, shatter, cloth, fluid, and tiled-deformation motion that works as authored video output rather than interactive website effects.

## Product constraints
- One Preset must render under every Pack and both native orientations.
- Every animation derives from explicit timestamp/frame/progress; no wall-clock or runtime randomness.
- Transparent compositions preserve premultiplied alpha and never paint undeclared backgrounds.
- Final output remains native 3840x2160 or 2160x3840; lower resolutions are allowed only for selected simulation/intermediate fields.
- CanvasUI is behavioral inspiration only. Implement from graphics fundamentals and WICG/WebGPU APIs with independent naming, parameters, shader code, and defaults.
- New Pipelines/domains require a verification Preset and Critic ACCEPT.

## Capability set
- Rebuild focal magnification as a credible optical lens with distortion, edge refraction, controlled chromatic dispersion, haze/frost, and optional Pack-resolved instrument chrome.
- Add non-fluted glass/frost vocabulary: smooth lens glass, frosted/transmission blur, droplets/bubble-style local refraction where compositionally justified.
- Add deterministic particle reveal/dissolve, 3D peel transition, seeded shatter transition, cloth/bend surface deformation, authored fluid/ripple simulation, 2D/3D asset-to-geometry exploration, and tiled deformation.
- Add shared engine seams for dirty DOM generations, pass-local bounds/quality, resource readiness, and seekable stateful GPU simulation where required.

## Done when
Every child epic/task is completed with tests, native horizontal+vertical proving renders, transparent-alpha verification where applicable, GUI schema/editor parity, updated current-truth docs/ADR, and Critic ACCEPT for each new Pipeline family verification Preset.
result: Completed the clean-room optical and deformation capability arc. Shipped rebuilt Magnify plus refractive-lens/frosted-glass optics; render-efficiency and readiness seams; typed particle-dissolve, sheet-peel, and seeded-shatter transitions; a deterministic fixed-step seek/reset/replay runtime; fluid-ripple, cloth-bend, and tiled-deformation Effects; GUI editors, schemas, fixtures, tests, and current-truth ADR/docs. ADR-0047 rejects broad asset-to-geometry import until a bounded Pipeline needs it. Independent Critics ACCEPTed the optical showcase and all six new transition/material/deformation fixtures at native horizontal and vertical. Final verification passed: git diff --check, npm run check, verify-presets, test:structural, build, test:browser, and npm test (75 files, 342 tests). description: Define automatic terminal routing, outcome mapping, profiling signals, receipt coverage, and non-gating failure semantics for Planning and Delivery.
result:
Defined the lifecycle observability contract:
- Observability is a required lifecycle stage before every terminal state, not a manual post-run command.
- Each outcome-specific observability stage runs one factory-specific workflow that first advances to the real terminal state, then invokes summary and the Sentry emitter as allowFailure steps. Sentry availability cannot alter the terminal outcome.
- Delivery covers done and aborted. Planning covers done, rejected, parked, failed-apply, failed-audit, and aborted; custom failure terminals retain their exact failedStage while the canonical broad outcome remains parked.
- The emitter remains the single network boundary and expands bounded metrics for stage visits/dispatches/time-to-gate, human touches, and failed terminal stage so Sentry supports profiling and diagnosis as well as completion counts.
- Both reusable profile compilers gain optional terminal-observer workflow configuration so materialization cannot erase the wiring and consumers without an observer remain backward compatible.
- A Swamp-native coverage method will compare every terminal state/journal key against emitter receipts. Missing coverage is explicit local data and a failing audit gate, not silent dashboard absence.
- Normal lifecycle verification must prove automatic receipt creation; direct invocation of the telemetry workflow is not acceptable evidence.
Architecture basis: Swamp workflows orchestrate multiple model methods; the emitter model owns the external Sentry action; reports remain deterministic analysis only, consistent with the Swamp architecture guide and docs/project-control-plane.md.
